title: Could the Whole Universe Be Alive and Evolving Like a Creature?
summary:
You know how animals and plants evolve over millions of years? Well, what if the entire universe evolves too? That's a wild idea some scientists are thinking about. They call it 'cosmological evolution.'

Here's the basic idea: black holes might be like eggs. When a black hole forms, it could squash matter into a super tiny point. Some physicists think that point might explode and create a brand-new universe! And that new universe might be a little bit different from its parent universe, just like baby animals are a little different from their parents.

If that happens over and over, universes could evolve. Universes that make lots of black holes would have more 'babies.' So over time, most universes would be really good at making black holes. Our universe might be one of those!

This idea isn't new. A physicist named Lee Smolin wrote about it back in 1992. He was inspired by other scientists who wondered if black holes could create new universes. But for a long time, not many people paid attention to Smolin's idea.

Then, a writer named Julian Gough found Smolin's work. Gough is famous for writing the story at the end of the video game Minecraft. He started thinking: our universe began as a hot ball of gas. Now it has stars, planets, and even life. That's a lot of complexity. How did that happen? Gough thinks evolution might be the answer.

Gough writes about this on his blog, The Egg and the Rock. He points out that the James Webb Space Telescope is finding surprising things about the early universe. Maybe those surprises fit with the idea that universes evolve.

Of course, this is just an idea. Scientists haven't proven it. But it's a fun thing to think about. If universes really do evolve, then our whole cosmos is like one giant living thing, growing and changing over unimaginable time. And maybe, somewhere out there, another universe is being born right now inside a black hole.
why_it_matters: Thinking about the universe evolving connects big ideas like black holes, life, and where we come from, and it can inspire you to ask questions scientists are still exploring.

Julian Gough is a writer known for creating the ending story of the video game Minecraft.

Article_Structure: WHO: Physicists like Lee Smolin and writer Julian Gough, plus other scientists who study the universe.
WHAT: The idea that black holes could create new baby universes, so the whole cosmos might evolve like living things.
WHERE: In space itself and in observations from the James Webb Space Telescope, which looks at the whole universe.
WHY: Because our universe started as a hot ball of gas and became complex with stars, planets, and life, and Gough thinks evolution may explain how that happened.
